system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the eighth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
A rectangular garden that is next to a building has a path around the other three sides, as shown.

[Image: Diagram of a garden and path next to a building]

What is the area of the path?

Figure, described in words:
A diagram shows a thick line labeled "Building" forming a vertical wall. Directly adjacent to the building wall is a shaded rectangular "Garden", surrounded on the remaining three sides by an unshaded "Path" forming a larger outer rectangle. The dimensions shown are: total vertical height of the outer rectangle along the building wall is 12 m; horizontal length of the garden is 10 m; vertical height of the garden is 8 m; and total horizontal width of the outer rectangle (garden plus path width) along the bottom is 12 m.

A. 144 m^2
B. 64 m^2
C. 44 m^2
D. 16 m^2

answer.description: The letter of the option you choose for the question.
answer.title: Answer

llm_thinking:
I'm trying to figure out the outer rectangle dimensions versus the garden area, since the building occupies one side and the path wraps around the other three. It seems like the outer rectangle should be 12 by 12 meters, with the garden taking up 10 by 8 meters adjacent to the building wall, so I'm working through how the path region fits into that remaining space.

Calculating: outer area 144, garden area 80, so the path area comes out to 64 — matching option B.
